transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I've been hearing things. Voices, mostly. It happens in my apartment, and sometimes when I'm at the museum, in the empty rooms. It sounds like... women, whispering from behind the walls. They tell me which photographs belong in the archive.
Have you experienced any periods where your mood felt unusually elevated, or conversely, periods where you felt deeply depressed or hopeless?

Well... sometimes. I have days where I feel... radiant, I suppose. Like I've been chosen. But... if anyone questions my plan, or tells me to slow down, I become furious. It just feels as if they are trying to erase me.
When you experience those periods of feeling 'radiant' or furious, do the voices occur only during those times, or do you hear them even when your mood feels completely normal?

No... they don't just happen then. 

There was... a stretch of time, maybe a few weeks, where I didn't feel that radiant energy. I wasn't... grand, or anything. I just felt normal. But I still heard the whispers in my apartment. And... I still knew the arts council people were tapping my phone lines. So, it's not just when my mood changes.
When you are speaking with others, do they ever tell you that your sentences don't make sense or that you are jumping between topics that aren't related?

Well... sometimes. My cousin complains about it. 

She'll ask a simple question, just about a bill or an appointment. And I try to answer her, but... I have to explain the grant first. And the shipping routes. My grandmother’s altar. It's all connected, you see. But... I suppose by the time I stop talking, nobody seems to know what I meant.

Looking back over the entire time you have been dealing with these voices and thoughts, would you say that the periods where your mood was very high or very low took up most of the time you were ill, or were they just a small part of the total time?

I suppose... it's most of the time. 

Ever since I retired, most of these months have been like that. Just... long stretches where I feel so driven. Like I've been chosen, and I just... I can't slow down. I get irritable. There are some quieter days, sometimes, where I just withdraw and keep to myself... but mostly, it's that driven feeling. It takes up most of it, yes.

During those 'quieter days' you mentioned, when your mood feels more neutral and you aren't feeling that 'driven' or 'radiant' energy, do you still hold the belief that the arts council is tapping your phone lines?

...Yes. Because it doesn't change just because I'm having a quiet day. 

I know the museum board and... the city arts people, they are monitoring my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and how it will change... how the galleries tell the truth. And no one has shown me a single thing that proves otherwise. So... yes. I still know it.
Have you ever experienced the voices or the belief about the arts council during a period of at least two weeks where you felt neither 'driven' or 'radiant', nor deeply depressed or hopeless?

Yes. 

A while ago... maybe a month or so. I wasn't feeling that energy. I was just... normal, I suppose. Not low, not high. But the whispers were still there in the apartment. And I still knew they were listening to the phone. It went on like that for a few weeks.
Looking back at the entire time you have been experiencing these voices and the belief about the arts council, has this been going on for at least six months?

Yes... it has. 

I suppose it's been... about eight months now. Since the voices started, and since I knew they were watching the archive. Yes.
